topAgencyDetails.agencyName: Department of Health and Human Services

forecast.forecastDesc:
The Award Ceiling for Year 1 is 0 (none). CDC anticipates an Approximate Total Fiscal Year Funding amount of $30,000,000 for Year 1, subject to the availability of funds.

This NOFO supports the Ministry of Health (MOH)-led digital transformation vision to modernize Uganda’s health data systems and infrastructure. It also supports enhancing capacity to provide timely epidemic intelligence for critical decision-making in HIV and related health programs. The data architecture is expected to encompass:

  • General and targeted surveys.
  • Clinical systems such as electronic medical records (EMR).
  • Digital registers.
  • Clinical indicator-based surveillance.
  • Disease surveillance.
  • Laboratory data.
  • Commodities, logistics, and pharmacy management information systems.
  • Community data.
  • Human resource management and development.
  • Other data collection activities to address existing data and knowledge gaps.

 

The NOFO also supports developing digital solutions and strengthening data warehousing, integration, and interoperability to build a sustainable and resilient digital ecosystem ready for transition to local governance.

opportunityHistoryDetails.opportunityTitle: Strengthening and modernizing sustainable public health systems and workforce in Uganda for data science, informatics, implementation science and surveys, and surveillance for timely, accurate, and integrated data for action under PEPFAR

forecast.forecastDesc:
The Award Ceiling for Year 1 is 0 (none). CDC anticipates an Approximate Total Fiscal Year Funding amount of $30,000,000 for Year 1, subject to the availability of funds.

​​This NOFO will focus on supporting the Ministry of Health (MOH)-led digital transformation vision to modernize health data systems and infrastructure, enhancing capacity to provide timely epidemic intelligence for critical decision-making in HIV and related health programs in Uganda. The data architecture will encompass general and targeted surveys and implementation science, clinical systems such as electronic medical records, digital registers, clinical indicator-based surveillance, disease surveillance, laboratory data, commodities/logistics/pharmacy management information systems, community data, human resource management and development, and other data collection activities to address existing data and knowledge gaps.

​​The NOFO will also support efforts for solutions development, data warehousing and integration, as well as central integration and interoperability solutions to facilitate a sustainable digital ecosystem.
